assessment.nobel_worthiness: Incretin physiology to GLP-1-based therapy is a coherent chain from hormone biology to a transformative treatment for type 2 diabetes and obesity, with large cardiometabolic outcome benefits. Originality and clinical and societal impact are exceptional.
assessment.attribution: Holst (GLP-1 physiology and secretion), Mojsov (identification of the active GLP-1 peptide forms) and Drucker (GLP-1 biology and translation) form a plausible trio. Knudsen's drug-development role is real, but the prize is limited to three, and credit relative to other pioneers is contested; I rely on my recollection of the history rather than independent verification.
assessment.maturity: Mechanism is confirmed across decades of independent physiology and multiple large clinical programmes; the field's impact is already visible, so recognition is timely and arguably overdue.
uncertainties: Allocation among Drucker, Holst, Mojsov and Knudsen is disputed and the supplied list may omit other key contributors.
Whether the committee frames the prize as basic hormone discovery or drug development is unresolved.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Rational inhibition of the BCR-ABL kinase turned chronic myeloid leukemia from a fatal disease into a manageable one and established the paradigm of targeted cancer therapy. Clarity of concept and lasting impact are very high.
assessment.attribution: Lydon (compound discovery and kinase-inhibitor programme), Druker (clinical proof of concept) and Sawyers (resistance mechanisms and next-generation inhibitors) is a natural three-way configuration. Credit within the original industry-academic effort could be argued, and I cannot verify every detail.
assessment.maturity: Over two decades of clinical follow-up with durable survival and replicated resistance biology; fully mature.
uncertainties: Industry team contributions beyond Lydon may complicate attribution.
The upstream BCR-ABL fusion discoveries are a separate chain and might be seen as needing their own recognition.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Engineered T-cell therapy has produced durable remissions in refractory B-cell malignancies and opened a new therapeutic modality. The discovery is clear, original, and clinically transformative.
assessment.attribution: June (clinical CAR-T translation in leukemia and lymphoma), Sadelain (CAR design with costimulation) and Rosenberg (adoptive cell transfer and early gene-engineered T cells) are credible; the original chimeric receptor concept by others such as Eshhar is not on this list, which weakens the configuration.
assessment.maturity: Multiple approved products and over a decade of follow-up; durability beyond hematologic cancers and toxicity are still evolving, but the core principle is solid.
uncertainties: Key early contributors to the CAR concept are not in the credited names.
Solid-tumour efficacy remains limited, which may temper perceived breadth.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: The unfolded protein response defined a new intracellular signalling logic from the endoplasmic reticulum to the nucleus, with broad relevance for proteostasis, secretory-cell physiology and disease. The discovery is elegant, original and has been highly influential.
assessment.attribution: Mori (HAC1/Ire1-dependent transcriptional response) and Walter (Ire1 and UPR mechanism, including later IRE1 and ISR work) is a clean two-person configuration with little credit ambiguity, as far as I recall.
assessment.maturity: Conserved from yeast to mammals and replicated for roughly thirty years; therapeutic translation (e.g. ISR modulators) is still developing but the basic discovery is mature.
uncertainties: Medical impact is more indirect than for the therapy-oriented candidates.
Others, such as Kohno and Cox, contributed to early UPR work and may be discussed.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Optogenetics gave neuroscience causal, cell-type-specific control of neural activity and transformed experimental physiology. Originality and methodological impact are very large, with growing translational use such as vision restoration.
assessment.attribution: Nagel and Hegemann (channelrhodopsin identification and characterisation) and Deisseroth (neuronal deployment and application) form a plausible trio; Boyden, Miesenböck and Bamberg also have strong claims, so allocation is genuinely contested.
assessment.maturity: Ubiquitous use across laboratories for fifteen years; clinical applications are early, but the tool's impact is established.
uncertainties: Six credited names for at most three seats makes the credit allocation contentious.
It is a method discovery, so the committee may weigh disease relevance differently.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: TOR/mTOR identification as the central controller of growth and nutrient response has reshaped cell biology, metabolism, ageing and cancer, and underlies rapalog therapies. Importance and breadth are high.
assessment.attribution: Hall (discovery of TOR as the genetic target) is central; Sabatini (mTOR and nutrient-sensing complexes) and Schreiber (rapamycin-FKBP12 chemical biology) contributed decisively, though other groups also cloned mTOR in parallel. Any configuration is debatable, and Sabatini's later professional controversies could affect committee views.
assessment.maturity: Pathway extensively replicated, with clinical use of rapamycin analogues; understanding is still being refined, but the core is stable.
uncertainties: Parallel discoveries by other groups (e.g. Heitman, Movva, Brown, Sabatini) complicate allocation.
Concerns about one candidate's conduct could affect a fair configuration.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: BCL-2 revealed that cancer can arise from blocked cell death, founding the concept of survival-gene oncogenes and leading to venetoclax and BH3-mimetic therapy. Both conceptual and clinical impact are strong.
assessment.attribution: Cory and Adams (cloning and characterisation of BCL-2 and its family) and Vaux (demonstration of its survival function) are plausible; Tsujimoto and Korsmeyer are among others with claims for the translocation and mechanism, and are not in the credited list.
assessment.maturity: Venetoclax approvals provide strong clinical validation after decades of independent work; the discovery is mature.
uncertainties: Early t(14;18) cloning by others is not credited here.
Apoptosis was recognised in 2002, which might temper the sense of novelty.

assessment.nobel_worthiness: Demonstrating that TNF is a therapeutic target in rheumatoid arthritis launched anti-cytokine therapy and changed treatment of several inflammatory diseases. The concept is clear and its impact on patients is large.
assessment.attribution: Feldmann and Maini jointly carried out the key mechanistic and clinical studies, giving a clean pair; other contributors in antibody engineering and TNF biology (e.g. Cerami, Vilcek, Kollias) may be raised.
assessment.maturity: Over twenty-five years of use, with multiple replicated agents and long-term outcome data; mature and arguably overdue.
uncertainties: TNF-biology contributors outside this list could be argued as essential.
I rely on memory of the history and have not verified details.
